questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Tight.
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of tightness varies by vehicle, so check your owner's manual.

questions.question: Fully-loaded trucks:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty trucks.
Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty trucks.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded trucks have a higher center of gravity. This makes them 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty trucks.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim the extinguisher at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible. Aim at the base of the fire, not the flames. If you are unsure which extinguisher to use or the fire involves hazardous materials, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine.
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure:

options.text: The tractor protection valve will close.
The rear trailer will detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve will close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the trailer's brakes if the trailer breaks away or leaks. When pressure in the emergency line drops, the valve closes and the trailer's emergency brakes activate.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it means:

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: A vehicle that pulls to one side when braking has a brake problem. Fix the problem before driving. Operating an unsafe vehicle violates federal and state laws.

questions.question: Before driving in winter, check:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Before winter driving, check your heat and defrost, coolant and antifreeze, wipers and washers, tire tread, chains, lights, reflectors, and exhaust system. Clear ice and snow from all windows, mirrors, steps, and the radiator. Make sure the winterfront is not closed too tight.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To make a normal stop with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you press, the more air pressure is released to stop the vehicle.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and could slow down other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
Wave an arm out of your window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with your emergency flashers activated.
questions.explanation: Use your emergency flashers to warn other drivers when driving slowly. Check your local laws to make sure emergency flashers are allowed.

questions.question: If you don't know how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you don't know what type of fire extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials fires, wait for firefighters to arrive. Let them put out the fire.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator to burn remaining fuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible if there is an engine fire. Do not open the hood when putting out the fire.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look at the signposts or signal housing at the crossing for emergency numbers. Call 911 or the appropriate emergency number.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle driver can:

options.text: Use any cell phone while driving.
Use only a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
Use a cell phone only on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
questions.explanation: You may only use a hands-free cell phone placed close to you while driving. Even hands-free phones are dangerous distractions. Know all cell phone laws in your state.

questions.question: In a vehicle with an automatic tractor protection valve, when does the valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air flow.

questions.question: Emergency air lines are usually what color?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red.
questions.explanation: Service air lines are blue. Emergency air lines are red.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every trip.
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before driving. Testing them before each trip helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system doesn't work properly?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may come out the back of the muffler.
It may cause problems with a full trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: When testing trailer emergency brakes, you should:

options.text: Pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency".

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency".
questions.explanation: Test trailer emergency brakes before starting a trip. Make sure the trailer rolls freely first. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or set it to "emergency." Pull forward slightly with the tractor. The trailer should not move.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slowly.
questions.explanation: Watch your vehicle's gauges before starting a trip. After you start the engine, the coolant temperature should rise gradually to the normal operating range.
